"I think once people are aware of it, they want the same sustainability standards for protecting our planet".

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

We live in the era of the satellite. They power our phones, banking infrastructure, navigational systems and internet, while providing stunning imagery and data that can be used to direct emergency services, feed weather forecasts and help coordinate military assets.

But low-Earth orbit is not an infinite resource. It's starting to get crowded, with over 16,000 satellites and over 1.2 million pieces of debris currently circling our planet at incredible speeds. And if not managed properly, the results could be catastrophic.

"In the early days of the space age actors could more or less ignore the other actors," Peter Martinez, executive director of the Secure World Foundation told Space.com. "You know the big sky paradigm, right? You can do what you want because the chances of your actions affecting others are minuscule."

As noted by Martinez, the modern orbital landscape is radically different from those early frontier days, especially since the mid 2010s and the advent of satellite megaconstellations. "Nowadays, we really do have to worry about orbital congestion, and because space is out of sight for most people, we don't."

Each new rocket launch leaves a footprint on the orbital environment, whether it be the satellite payloads they place in orbit or the pieces of inert hardware they leave behind such as an interstage adapter or rocket body. All of those objects create an ever-increasing risk of collisions.

In a worst case scenario, clouds of debris spawned by colliding spacecraft could create a cascading effect known as the Kessler syndrome, with the potential to render the orbital environment completely unusable, trapping us on Earth.

Enter King Charles III's Astra Carta, an all-encompassing roadmap to space exploration that launched on June 28, 2023 with a clear but ambitious mandate — to place sustainability at the core of humanity's presence beyond Earth.

The Astra Carta stands as the space-focused sibling of the Terra Carta — a voluntary framework that launched in 2021 with the goal of safeguarding Earth's natural splendor by championing a transition to global sustainability practices and environmental responsibility.

Both names were chosen to draw comparison with the Magna Carta, a royal charter that served as an early foundation for the English Legal system and modern day democracies. The principles enshrined in the Astra Carta have the potential to be similarly transformative if taken to heart.

"I have long felt that protecting space that immediately surrounds our planet is one of those issues few recognize as important, but like so many of our present challenges, that were ignored for too long, if we do not address it quickly, it will come back to haunt us in a big way," the then-Prince of Wales stated in a message to participants of the 4th Summit for Space Sustainability in June 2022.

The framework was crafted by King Charles III's Sustainable Markets Initiative (SMI), which drew on the expertise of academics, heads of national space agencies and experts, such as Canadian astronaut and former International Space Station commander Chris Hadfield.

"It's like Stephen Hawking said, 'Stop looking at your shoes and look up'," Hadfield told Space.com. "It's really easy to spend a bunch of time on the news of the day, or the news of the week, or even the news of the month, you actually need something aspirational to be able to look up to some external measure of long-term success and goodness."

To Hadfield, the Astra Carta is an example of just that. It encourages humanity to embrace a global, peaceful outlook, which the astronaut believes will be vital to humanity's success as we venture deeper into space.

"If you view the moon as an eighth continent, which essentially it is, bigger than Africa, untapped, largely unsurveyed, whose laws are we going to follow as we begin to settle there?" continued Hadfield. "Or do we just transport kind of a silly imprint of our current geopolitics?"

The Astra Carta addresses a variety of interconnected challenges over its 33 pages and the 13 Articles of its "Zero Draft", which compliments and builds on the goals of existing treaties like the UN Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space, and the U.S. Artemis Accords.

Article 8 primarily focuses on orbital debris mitigation, and encourages the use of reusable launchers and responsible satellite disposal, investing in debris removal, and boosting public knowledge of the threat through education, among other measures.

But the Astra Carta's systemic approach reaches far beyond the threat posed by space debris. The remaining 12 articles highlight a latticework of forward thinking actions, ranging from the need for greater co-ordination between satellite operators to encouraging the development of novel propulsion and life support systems.It also calls for ethical guidelines on the use of AI in space, the establishing of key performance indicators for sustainability and legal frameworks for cybersecurity while advocating for treaties that prohibit the use of automated weapons in space, and so much more.

Each topic addressed in the Astra Carta looms large enough on its own. Taken together, they appear borderline insurmountable. But the convening power of King Charles III's SMI could prove to be a powerful factor in addressing them.

"What's interesting with the space economy is that the players within it are very fragmented, all over the world, and there isn't something that's sort of telling them what to do and how to behave in space," Sustainable Markets Initiative (SMI) CEO Jennifer Jordan-Saifi told Space.com. "And so there's definitely an appetite from all of those private sector players across the world … for something to galvanise common purpose."

To that end, the SMI has created a Space Sustainability Task Force to champion the principles of the Astra Carta, led by an advisory council that includes European Space Agency director Josef Aschbacher, UK Space Agency Director Paul Bate, Martinez and Hadfield.

The non-profit has advanced the goals of the Astra Carta at meetings of the United Nations Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space and by working with major players, including SpaceX. It also organizes high profile events such as the Nov. 7 Artemis Celebration Gala at the Kennedy Space Center, Florida, which honored Artemis II astronauts Reid Wiseman, Jeremy Hansen and Victor Glover while bringing together 450 leaders and pioneers from the space, government and business sectors.

In July earlier this year, His Majesty opened the UK Space and Defence Gateway at the Harwell Science and Innovation Campus in Oxfordshire, which partnered with the SMI and created an investment council to further the principles of the framework.

The Astra Carta's champions are actively engaging the private sector, governments and other luminaries. What's more, Jordan-Saifi believes that the voluntary nature of the Astra Carta could trigger widespread change faster than may be possible through the traditional U.N. system, which may need to be incorporated into country-level laws in a process that could take decades.

"The voluntary framework is the fastest way to get everyone on the same page. And then we might move to more concrete and enforceable, binding options in the future." In the meantime, Jordan-Saifi hopes that players in the space industry will play a role in holding one another accountable to observing the principles of the Astra Carta.

But could the competitive nature of the emerging space sector act as a barrier to embracing sustainability, as commercial entities race to capture their own share of the market?

But could the competitive nature of the emerging space sector act as a barrier to embracing sustainability, as commercial entities race to capture their own share of the market?

"Space has become a very congested and competitive domain, and I don't, frankly, see the big players taking their foot off the gas, both for commercial and for strategic reasons," explained Martinez. "But I think that there is a growing awareness of the fragility of the space domain, and so, therefore, I would expect the major actors to recognise this and to behave responsibly."

Martinez points to SpaceX's Starlink constellation as an example of good behavior on orbit, with the company often sharing satellite trajectories and maneuver plans for other actors to see and plan for ahead of time. "...This is what I think we are all aspiring towards in the future, some form of global, globally coordinated, or global space traffic coordination system. which we don't yet have today."

A heightened risk comes from newcomers drawn to the growing space economy from other sectors. "They don't understand that they're entering a fragile and strategic domain, and that's where initiatives like the Astra Carta can help to socialise this awareness," continued Martinez.

But one of the greatest potential strengths of the Astra Carta may rest with its unique ability to engage the public and raise awareness in the quest for sustainability in space, as much as its capacity to galvanise the private sector.

"The first step is to create social awareness of this, and I would say that one of the values of the Astra Carta is the cachet of royal attention to this issue," said Martinez. "Extending the king's already well known appreciation for stewardship of the Earth environment to the orbital environment. And I think that is the real value of it … if the king is talking about this issue, [it] raises its salience and gets others to think about it."

In this, His Majesty is supported by the SMI and a team of astronaut ambassadors, including Hadfield, U.S. astronaut Nicole Stott and ESA astronaut Tim Peake.

"We're going to Antigua and Barbuda for the heads of government meeting of the Commonwealth, and the king attends that, and we're actually bringing Chris Hadfield on stage to talk to the 2.7 billion citizens of the Commonwealth about the AstraCarta," said Jordan-Saifi touting the SMI's ability to reach a vast global audience. "...We really want more and more people to be involved and be aware about space. And I think once people are aware of it, they want the same sustainability standards for protecting our planet."

However, the sheer scope of the Astra Carta makes it a challenge to communicate to the public. Potential readers may also be surprised to find that the most up-to-date version available on the SMI website is still the "Zero Draft" — the name commonly given to unpolished works not yet ready for publication.

Jordan-Saifi assured me that the Astra Carta's Zero Draft is still relevant and accurate, but that a version 1.0 is currently going through consultation for potential release in the future.

Which begs the question: how would one even gauge the success of so far reaching a roadmap as the Astra Carta? Its voluntary nature makes it inherently challenging, but as Jordan-Saifi notes, there are certain metrics that could be used to indicate how far the Astra Carta has shifted the space economy towards sustainability in the future.

The SMI could track the number of countries and commercial partners that have agreed to adhere to the principles of the Astra Carta, assess public awareness and gauge the success with which its tenants have been formally adopted by the United Nations and other regulatory bodies.

Hadfield, meanwhile, reflected on the difficulties facing the Astra Carta's champions on the long road to sustainability.

"How do you weave in the role of a space agency who has to answer to the national demands and the constraints that they have, both financially and politically?" questioned the former astronaut. "And how do you weave in all of the nonprofits that have all different agendas? The Astra Carta is trying to do all those things, and I think it's done admirably, but it takes patience. And if you're ready to declare anything after three years, you're making a mistake."

Want to know more? Then be sure to head over to the SMI website to read the Astra Carta in full, or you can read a recent op-ed on whether we are currently on track for true space sustainability.

Anthony Wood joined Space.com in April 2025 after contributing articles to outlets including IGN, New Atlas and Gizmodo. He has a passion for the night sky, science, Hideo Kojima, and human space exploration, and can’t wait for the day when astronauts once again set foot on the moon.

#814. S.W.A.T. Star Larry Poindexter Dead at 66 After Being Hit by a Car

Larry Poindexter—known for roles in the film S.W.A.T, and TV shows Days Of Our Lives, The Hard Times of RJ Berger, JAG and more—died on Nov. 18 at the age of 66 after being struck by a car.

Hollywood is mourning the loss of a veteran actor.

Larry Poindexter—best known for starring in the 2003 film S.W.A.T.—died on Nov. 18, his rep Adam Levine confirmed to E! News. He was 66.

“Larry was someone who was incredibly kind and loving to his family, friends and strangers alike,” Levine said. “A true artist who was devoted to his craft, Larry took great joy in entertaining and informing through his performances.”

Poindexter died four days after being struck by a car in Los Angeles, according to NBC News, citing police and the late actor's agent Harry Gold.

Poindexter—who shared twin sons with his wife Carol Kritzer—had been picking up food in his Studio City neighborhood on Nov. 13, before he was hit by a car while crossing the street, per the outlet.

The General Hospital alum was subsequently hospitalized and was set to undergo surgery for his broken ribs on Nov. 18, but he died suddenly, according to Gold.

Poindexter’s agent told NBC News that doctors did not believe his injuries were “anything serious,” adding, “They put him in the hospital for observation and to repair some broken bones and then he passed away.”

Along with his role as LAPD Captain Tom Fuller in S.W.A.T., Poindexter, who had nearly 200 acting credits throughout his career, was also known for his stints on soap operas Days Of Our Lives, Santa Barbara and General Hospital. He also held a recurring role on the '90s legal drama JAG.

In more recent years, he appeared on The Hard Times of RJ Berger. His costar on the MTV comedy Paul Iacono was among those who expressed their grief after Pointdexter’s untimely death.

“I’m heartbroken by the loss of Larry Poindexter, my dad on RJ Berger,” Iacono wrote in a Nov. 19 Instagram post alongside throwback photos with his on-screen dad. “Few people I’ve known were as kind, generous, fiercely talented, and f--king hilarious. Above all, Larry was a GOOD egg.”

The 38-year-old shared that Poindexter “looked out” for him in his early 20s, writing that he “offered wisdom I wasn’t always ready to hear,” and “taught me that being a good person and collaborator mattered just as much as being a great actor.”

As he concluded his emotional post, Iacono emphasized that he’ll never forget his time sharing the screen with Poindexter.

“I’m forever honored to have played his son,” he wrote, “and I’ll always cherish him as my second father.”

Armed with bonus scenes and extras, Marvel Studios' updated version of its 2019 blockbuster just landed on Disney+

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Disney and Marvel Studios have a lot riding on "Avengers: Doomsday," and they’re pulling out all the stops to make sure audiences are well-prepared to experience the alt-universe battle royale when it drops on December 18.

After a successful limited theater run earlier this fall, Marvel Studios just dropped "Avengers: Endgame Encore" onto Disney+. So, if you missed this beefed-up extended rerelease in theaters, you can still experience all the extra content that ties directly into the upcoming "Avengers: Doomsday."

"Endgame's" recent theatrical return came on Sept. 25, 2026, earned $86 million, and included four bonus scenes totaling roughly four minutes and a special "Doomsday" preview. The rerelease also took it back to the pinnacle of the all-time box office peak by passing "Avatar."

The $356 million sequel to 2018's "Avengers: Infinity War" closed out The Infinity Saga, and the two-part spectacle became widely known as the high-water mark of the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

"Avengers: Endgame Encore" will also be included in Disney+'s signature "Countdown to Avengers: Doomsday" collection, a curated roundup of former Marvel shows and movies to study up on. If you haven't been keeping up with the MCU, you've got plenty of homework to do ahead of "Avengers: Doomsday."

With its charismatic cast of dozens and the triumphant MCU return of Robert Downey Jr., this time portraying the metal-masked Victor Von Doom, expectations are sky-high that this might reignite the glory days and usher in a brave new world for bored superhero-loving cinephiles.

"Avengers: Endgame Encore" is now on Disney+.

#812. Kelly Osbourne Looks Unrecognizable With Long Dark Hair Transformation

Kelly Osbourne channeled Ariel from The Little Mermaid as she rocked long auburn hair during the ZYN Rolling Stone U.K. Awards: "You want thingamabobs?"

Kelly Osbourne wants to be where the people are.

So much so, the Osbournes alum channeled Ariel from The Little Mermaid with a dark red hair transformation for her Nov. 19 appearance at the ZYN Rolling Stone U.K. Awards.

Osbourne—who has been rocking a blonde, shoulder-length hair in recent months—stepped out with long, auburn tresses, which she styled in loose waves. She paired the look with a shimmery, ocean blue gown from Rebecca Vallance and gold jewelry.

Sharing a selfie set to "Part of Your World," the 42-year-old wrote on her Instagram Story in reference to the Disney song, "It's give.. you want thingamabobs I got 20."

But this wasn't the first time Osbourne flipped her fins in a new 'do this year. In September, the former Fashion Police host debuted a jet black wig featuring blunt asymmetric bangs while walking in designer Natasha Zinko's London Fashion Week.

Osbourne explained that she's been playing around with faux hairpieces since experiencing extreme weight loss in the wake of her dad Ozzy Osbourne's 2025 death.

“I looked like the f--king Crypt Keeper," she admitted in a September interview with The Mail on Sunday. “I said, 'This is scary. I didn't know I looked like this.’"

"I wore a wig to cover my face, so you couldn't see how skinny my cheekbones really were," Osbourne continued, explaining how her stylists were "trying to find clothes to not make me look skinnier" as she navigated her grief. "My spine—you could see every single bone."

However, she's since developed a healthier relationship with her body, recently sharing that she's gained back 30 lbs.

“I didn’t know that I looked like that until I saw the pictures,” she told The Sun last month of her weight loss photos. “When I saw them, I couldn’t f--king believe it. I was as shocked as everyone else.”

#811. We'll only sell if offer makes club blink - McInnes

Derek McInnes joined Rangers from Hearts in the summer

Manager Derek McInnes says Rangers will only sell a player in the January transfer window if they receive an offer that "makes the club blink".

Players such as German striker Ryan Naderi, Mauritania winger Djeidi Gassama and Belgium midfielder Nico Raskin have been linked with moves while centre-backs Olwethu Makhanya and Emmanuel Fernandez have attracted interest after their starts to the season.

However McInnes will oppose moves for players who have featured regularly in his first season in charge at Ibrox - unless a club makes a startling offer that is too good to turn down.

"If somebody comes in way over the top then you have to obviously consider these sort of things," he said.

"But in the main, we're not looking to move players out, particularly players that have been playing regularly. We want to shut that down really early.

"We don't want agents flirting with clubs, giving them any encouragement. We know and understand that keeping that core of players and having that stability is so important for us.

"We don't want January window to be excitable or dramatic. Just to come and go and hopefully we can just keep doing what we're doing."

McInnes said that Lawrence Shankland and Cammy Devlin are progressing well in their rehabilitation and that his players returned unscathed from international duty - although Kevin Kelsy was back later than expected from the Venezuela squad.

"Kevin is the only wee anomaly. We didn't get him back from Russia on Wednesday night because of a few issues with transport, but we managed to get him back in at lunchtime on Thursday," McInnes said.

Rangers face Motherwell in Lanarkshire on Saturday and have a solid away record - but dropped points in two away draws prior to the win at St Mirren.

McInnes is expecting a stiff test as he believes the Steelmen are beginning to perform like the side that impressed throughout last season and qualified for Europe.

"I think they have got a lot of traits and similarities to the team that got a lot of success last year. I think over the last two or three games they've started to look a wee bit more like that," he added.

"They'll be a difficult opponent, but if we want to get to where we want to get to this season, we want to make sure we leave Motherwell with all three points."

#810. 'I'm very healthy' - Kompany to return to dugout after health scare

Kompany was appointed Bayern Munich manager in May 2024

Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany says he is "very healthy" and grateful for all of the support he has received as he prepares to return to the dugout on Friday.

The 40-year-old former Manchester City captain was taken to hospital after falling ill while watching the club's second team train last month.

Kompany was diagnosed with meningeal irritation - an inflammation of the protective membrane surrounding the brain and spinal cord.

Speaking at a news conference on Thursday he thanked the club, medical staff, players, coaches and fans for their support.

"At the time, it was a new experience. Looking back, everything went perfectly. I received support right away, from the club and the doctors. I'm very grateful.

"You try to stay calm and wait until you have the results. It was a positive process, all the tests were positive.

"I have to say, I'm very healthy. We did a lot of tests, and they all came back fine. In those quiet moments, you also try to learn.

"Now I feel very good again and I'm happy to be back with the team."

While he has been recovering Kompany's assistant Aaron Danks has led the side to four wins and a draw.

"I'd also like to thank the coaching community," Kompany added. "We're always competing, but almost every coach has reached out to me, even if we've played against each other and perhaps argued as well. That's a beautiful thing."

Bayern, for whom England captain Harry Kane has been in fine form, are top of the Bundesliga, level on points with Borussia Dortmund.

Defending champions Bayern face Cologne on Friday after the end of the two-week international break.

#809. Iran denies role in fridge hack, France summons ambassador

France has said it rules "nothing" out in response to a cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration units. Iran, however, said it categorically rejected Paris' "baseless and one-sided accusations" of IRGC involvement.

Iran on Tuesday dismissed French accusations that its Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) was behind a cyberattack on hundreds of supermarkets last month, as Paris summoned Tehran's ambassador to discuss the incident.

"Iran's Foreign Ministry categorically rejects the French government's baseless and one-sided accusations against Iran regarding alleged cyber activities in France," the ministry said, adding that it "strongly condemns this hackneyed policy of leveling accusations against the Islamic Republic."

The alleged attack, which began overnight on October 11-12, raised the temperatures in supermarket refrigerators and freezer units, spoiling produce and even causing fires in isolated instances.

A series of similar incidents have since followed in Europe and beyond, even including a failed attack on cooling units at French blood banks this month, though it is not yet clear if these subsequent events are connected.

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said on Tuesday that his government would "rule nothing out and will take all measures — including those we may not disclose publicly — that we deem proportionate and necessary to deter any further attacks."

Barrot was speaking amid a G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris that included discussions with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on the conflict with Iran.

Barrot even said that despite a change in tone from the Trump administration since the midterm election defeat in the US, the risk of a renewed escalation with Iran could not be ruled out, "otherwise, we would not have devoted so much time and energy over the past two days to addressing these issues with our American counterpart."

France summoned the Iranian ambassador on Tuesday and said it would be seeking European-level sanctions in response.

The EU said it would seek to provide a "swift and united response" pending discussion with member states.

"As the EU, we have consistently called on all states to refrain from malicious behavior in the cyberspace, and we will continue to address such malicious behavior, making use of all the tools that we have, also under the EU cyber diplomacy toolbox, including sanctions," spokesman Anouar El Anouni said.

Barrot said that the goal of any response would be "to deter anyone who might be tempted, in Iran or elsewhere, to do it again."

Tehran appeared to threaten retaliatory measures of its own if sanctions materialized, saying it would "not hesitate to take necessary and appropriate measures to safeguard its national interests and security in the face of unlawful foreign activities."

It accused France of "merely projecting its own governance failures" with its allegations.

"A government that cannot even manage the temperature of its own refrigerators now seeks to shift the blame onto foreign actors through these preposterous accusations," it said.

Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said on Monday that she had opened an investigation into leading members of Shahid Kaveh, a cyber unit that is part of Iran's multi-force specialist military, the IRGC, that answers directly to its religious leadership.

She said her office had requested arrest warrants against two Shahid Kaveh officials and was investigating others.

She described the entity as "an offensive cyber unit affiliated with the Electronic and Cyber Center of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps."

French cyber intelligence agencies said the unit conducted "large-scale campaigns targeting industrial equipment for the purpose of sabotage." It said it primarily targeted Israel and the US, but also France and other European countries.

Beccuau said that the attack targeted roughly 700 of France's roughly 10,000 supermarkets. It used web interfaces to "initiate abnormal, indefinite defrost cycles," and also to disable automated alerts from sensors designed to go off when temperatures exceeded certain levels.

Sweden's Civil Defense Minister Carl-Oskar Bohlin warned that more cyberattacks could be expected in the coming months, as AI tools make it easier to detect and exploit vulnerabilities.

He said that it was not yet possible to say if hacks targeted Swedish supermarkets last week were connected, not least because the type of sabotage would have "been easy to copy" after seeing the initial reports in October.

#808. Fiona the Hippo Dies Days After Eating Visitor’s Hat

Fiona the Hippo has died after accidentally eating a visitor's hat that was thrown into her enclosure, the Cincinnati Zoo confirmed: "She fought until she couldn’t anymore.”

The Cincinnati Zoo has suffered an enormously devastating loss.

Fiona the Hippo—who first gained fame in 2017 after being born six weeks premature—has died after accidentally eating a visitor’s hat earlier this month, the Cincinnati Zoo confirmed.

“We are in shock at the moment,” the zoo’s director Dave Jenike said in a Nov. 19 press release. “We did not expect this outcome.  She fought until she couldn’t anymore.”

According to the zoo, the veterinary staff tried everything they could to save the 9-year-old hippo as they attempted to move the knit hat out of her system.

“Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn’t fight anymore,” Jenike added. “She was dearly loved by her Zoo family and countless others around the world. Her loss will be felt deeply by so many.”

The Ohio zoo asked the public to “keep the people who worked with Fiona and tried to save her in your thoughts and prayers.”

The Nile hippopotamus’ health woes began on Nov. 8 when she accidentally swallowed a hat that a zoo visitor had thrown in the air, which a ceiling fan then moved into her enclosure, zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley had confirmed to the Associated Press.

Prior to her passing, the Cincinnati Zoo had been hopeful about her odds, saying in a Nov. 17 Facebook post that they were “monitoring her around the clock” and were “cautiously optimistic that she will pass it and return to her usual self.”

Fiona—who would have turned 10 in January—also received a colonoscopy, courtesy of the Columbus Zoo, as well as an ultrasound, which showed that her intestines were bunching, proving that she was working on passing something through her body.

Much like her death, Fiona’s birth was difficult, as she was born six weeks premature in 2017, weighing in at just 25 pounds, the lowest recorded birth weight for her species ever. She quickly became a celebrity across the internet as zoo staffers shared her progress with the world and less than two months later reached 90 pounds.

“Fiona was such a gift,” Cincinnati Zoo Executive Chair of the Board Thane Maynard shared Nov. 19. “I have never known an animal so beloved in all my life. From the day she was born, she was like lightning in a bottle. And, she will be remembered and beloved many years from now.”

For a look back at Fiona’s larger than life moments, keep reading.

The zoo's 17-year-old hippo named Bibi gave birth to little Fiona six weeks early on January 24, 2017. She weighed 25 lbs. less than the lowest recorded birth weight for her species, prompting critical care from vet staff.

Fiona's health made steady improvements in the weeks after her arrival, and by mid-March she had reached the 90 lb. mark, was eating hay and enjoying time in the pool!

Ever so curious about her surroundings, Fiona couldn't help but get an up-close look at herself on a computer screen.

By May, Fiona was well into the 200 lb. range and spending plenty of time lounging in her kiddie pool. What. A. Life.

Thanks to Fiona's tireless spirit and determination, she graduated to deeper-level pools after learning how to propel herself through the water.

It wasn't until early June that little Fiona began spending time with her mama. In the beginning, Bifi (as they were so lovingly dubbed) interacted during brief, supervised play dates but have since begun adjusting to life in the outdoor pool enclosure.

Fiona's dad Henry was reunited with his daughter one month later and from the looks of those hippo grins, their first time interacting went swell!

Fiona embraces all her curves and all her edges, and it's a much-needed reminder that we all should too.

It took much longer than anticipated, but Henry, Bibi and Fiona are finally cohabitating as a happy and healthy bloat. She can't get enough time exploring her dads' mouth, which is apparently normal behavior for a growing baby hippo!

Without a finalized schedule in place, Cincinnati Zoo visitors should cross their fingers in anticipation of seeing Fiona out and about. Here she is laying a wet one on her caregiver. Mwah!

This mother-daughter pair spends their afternoons splashing in the pool like any hippos should. And aren't those faces priceless?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Dream Chaser space plane just cleared a major hurdle ahead of its planned spring 2027 spaceflight debut.

Dream Chaser just received U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) approval for its return to Earth on that robotic mission, either at the space shuttle landing facility at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida or at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.

"Thank you to the FAA for its collaboration and support of commercial space innovation," representatives of Sierra Space, the Colorado company that builds Dream Chaser, wrote on X on Monday (Nov. 9).

The FAA's environmental assessment found that Dream Chaser "would not significantly impact the quality of the human environment" under the National Environmental Policy Act, the agency stated. (It should also be noted that the U.S. has lately been suggesting that environmental laws should be bypassed to meet quickly rising demand for launches and landings.)

For example, for a potential return at Vandenberg, "sonic booms are anticipated but would be temporary, short in duration, and limited to 1.1 PSF [pounds per square foot] or less, which is similar to a thunderclap," the FAA stated.

The 30-foot-long (9 meters) Dream Chaser has been in development for more than two decades. It has yet to launch to space, though it has completed a couple of drop tests from the air. Dream Chaser was an entrant in NASA's Commercial Crew series of contracts to ferry astronauts to and from the International Space Station (ISS), but it didn't end up making the cut; in 2014, NASA picked Boeing's Starliner and SpaceX's Crew Dragon to provide this taxi service.

The following year, Sierra Nevada Corporation — then the entity in charge of Dream Chaser — unveiled a cargo version of the space plane. In 2016, NASA selected the company to conduct at least six uncrewed cargo flights to the ISS, but development delays repeatedly pushed those missions into the future.

Dream Chaser was originally expected to fly those robotic resupply missions on United Launch Alliance's workhorse Atlas V rocket. A few years ago, however, the space plane switched over to Vulcan Centaur, the successor to the venerable Atlas V.

Dream Chaser was supposed to ride on Vulcan's second-ever mission but wasn't ready in time, so that flight went ahead in October 2024 without the space plane. Sierra Space is now targeting spring 2027 for Dream Chaser's first liftoff, which will be a free-flying test mission in Earth orbit.

The company is now pursuing many types of contracts for Dream Chaser, anticipating a mix of missions for NASA, the U.S. military and private companies — including the consortiums that plan to build commercial space stations. Indeed, Sierra Space is a member of one such consortium — the group that plans to build an outpost known as Orbital Reef.

Elizabeth Howell (she/her), Ph.D., was a staff writer in the spaceflight channel between 2022 and 2024 specializing in Canadian space news. She was contributing writer for Space.com for 10 years from 2012 to 2024. Elizabeth's reporting includes multiple exclusives with the White House, leading world coverage about a lost-and-found space tomato on the International Space Station, witnessing five human spaceflight launches on two continents, flying parabolic, working inside a spacesuit, and participating in a simulated Mars mission. Her latest book, "Why Am I Taller?" (ECW Press, 2022) is co-written with astronaut Dave Williams.

#806. Will this be the tightest Championship promotion race ever?

The top five teams in the Championship are separated by just one point

Many supporters often like to label the Championship "the best league in the world".

It might be a throwaway comment, but it is one founded on the premise that the level of unpredictability and drama is unmatched.

And there is a case to be made that the Championship is living up to its unofficial tag more than ever this season.

We have seen astonishing comebacks, goals galore, unexpected results - and one third of the way through the 2026-27 campaign, you could throw a blanket over the top half of the table.

With just one point between the top five sides and eight points separating leaders Birmingham City down to Blackburn Rovers in 13th after 15 games, is this shaping up to be one of, if not the best promotion and play-off contests ever in the second tier?

A total of 12 different teams have been in a Championship play-off spot since gameweek four

"This is going to be fun," said 72+ EFL podcast host Aaron Paul.

Jobi McAnuff, who won the Championship with Reading in 2011-12, agrees.

"It's been a brilliant start of the season. I think there's such a lovely open nature to the league so far," McAnuff said.

"You certainly wouldn't have expected West Brom right up there. Stoke... Mark Robins again doing brilliantly, and Birmingham sitting top of the table."

Former Bromley manager Andy Woodman described it as "anyone's league".

"This Championship is relentless," Woodman said. "I'm looking at all the clubs in there and Scott Parker's record of getting out of the league. He's now at West Ham sitting just behind them ready to come up.

"It is going to be an unbelievable finish to the season and if we were to call it, I don't think we could."

The final game before the two-week international break epitomised just how close the race is, and gives us plenty of reason for excitement when the Championship returns this weekend.

It is usually a rare and precious moment when football fans are able to serenade their heroes with 'We are top of the league' on the terraces.

But no less than four sets of supporters were able to do so in the space of a few hours on the afternoon of Saturday, 7 November.

The name at the top of the table changed eight times between 12:54 GMT and 16:51 GMT that day, with Birmingham eventually securing pole position.

That was only after Wolves, Stoke and Middlesbrough had led the way, however briefly, earlier in the day.

The table after 15 games is as tight as it has been since Opta started compiling statistics in 2004, although there is one other season in which just one point separated the top five sides beyond this point in a campaign, and boy, was it a doozy.

In early March 2015 Roy Hodgson was still England manager and Prime Minister David Cameron led a Conservative/Lib Dem coalition in Westminster.

Meanwhile, 36 games into the Championship season, this is what the title race looked like...

Bournemouth and Watford won automatic promotion in 2014-15, with Norwich going up via the play-offs

Bournemouth went on to pick up 24 points from their final 10 games to win the title and promotion to the top flight for the first time with 90 points, one ahead of Watford, who also went up.

Norwich and Middlesbrough had to settle for the play-offs, finishing third and fourth on 86 and 85 points respectively, while Brentford and Ipswich sneaked into the play-offs on goal difference, with Wolves missing out after also finishing on 78 points.

Derby ended up in eighth after taking only 17 points from their final 10 games to miss the play-offs by a point.

The table only tells half the story, however.

The Hornets would have been champions had they not conceded a late equaliser against Sheffield Wednesday on the final afternoon while the Rams had just needed to avoid defeat to secure a top-six finish, only to go down 3-0 at home to lowly Reading.

We can only hope 1 May 2027 provides us with half as much drama on the final day of the regular season.

Three points separated the top five teams in the Championship after 15 games in 2014-15

With eight play-off places now up for grabs, the odds are it might even exceed it.

And we can all take heart from the fact the table now is slightly tighter than the one in 2014-15 was after 15 games, while it's worth noting that only one of those top five fell away in the run-in.

Does that suggest our three promoted sides will come from the current top five?

The Championship's top goalscorer Will Lankshear has netted 13 of the 532 goals across 180 games in the division so far this season

If you want lots of goals and a tense battle at the top, then look no further than the Championship.

No other league in Europe is as tightly contested right now.

The Dutch Eredivisie comes closest with three points separating the top five, compared to just one point in the Championship.

However, the season is only nine games old in the Netherlands, as opposed to 15 in the English second tier.

Only two points separate the top four in the Belgian Pro League after 11 matches but there is a nine-point gap from first to fifth.

And it is not just the promotion race delivering so far this season - the entire division is coming up with the goods in terms of entertainment.

The last time goals were banged in at a higher rate in the second tier, England were about to win the World Cup for the first and only time to date.

This season's ratio of 2.96 goals per game is the highest in the 60 years since there were 3.08 per game across the 1965-66 campaign.

With 532 goals already netted in the Championship, we are on course for a total of 1,633 should the trend continue.

That would be the highest number of goals achieved at this level since 1957-58 when there were 1,637.

The highest number of goals ever in the second tier was in 1926-27, when there were 22 teams in the division and fewer games played overall (462) compared to today (552).

Third-placed Stoke City have only been given a 5.26% chance of automatic promotion by Opta (data correct as of 19 November)

Predicting the completely unpredictable might be a futile task, particularly this season.

But Opta's Supercomputer has tried to do just that by crunching the numbers to estimate the likely outcome of every remaining match using its power rankings tool and betting odds.

Opta's model considers the strength of opponents and simulates the remaining fixtures thousands of times.

The results? Middlesbrough will win the title with Wolves gaining the second automatic promotion spot.

Birmingham, Stoke, West Brom and Southampton are predicted to finish in the play-offs, as are Swansea, though they will have to do so without boss Vitor Matos who has left for French Ligue 1 club Strasbourg, while Opta expect West Ham to replace QPR in the top eight.

Woodman believes Parker's experience will help the Hammers recover from their recent blip, which prompted the club to sack boss Nuno Espirito Santo and replace him with their former midfielder.

"He knows this league inside out," said Woodman. "I'd be hard pressed to say who's better equipped for getting teams out of this league than Scotty Parker.

"He's a phenomenal manager and I think he'll do really well at West Ham."

McAnuff believes Middlesbrough are the ones to beat.

"I love what Kim Hellberg's done," he said. "They've missed Will Lankshear the past couple of games, but I still have them as my favourites. I think anyone who's above them this year will be getting automatically promoted."

Four of the teams currently in the race will meet in the first game after the international break when Stoke host Birmingham and West Brom visit Swansea.

"One of those, maybe two, will really look at it and go: 'Why can't we be the Coventry this season?'" added McAnuff.

"There's no reason why Birmingham - with such an open start to the league, particularly going down to eight teams this year - can't at least get into the play-offs.

"They will have designs on staying higher, I'm sure of that, but I do think some of the bigger teams are going to come good later on in the season."

#805. From Forest fringes to Glasner's go-to guy - the rise of McAtee

James McAtee made six appearances for Manchester City after coming through the academy

"James McAtee is probably one of the winners of this pre-season."

Oliver Glasner's immediate impression of his Nottingham Forest midfielder foretold the faith the head coach has shown in him.

Forest appear to have found their Elliot Anderson replacement from within as McAtee has become a key man for the Austrian.

After his Â£30m move from Manchester City in 2025, McAtee endured a difficult start to life at the City Ground.

Yet he played a key role as Forest toppled City and the returning Anderson before the international break for their first home win of the season.

There has been no clamour for an England call, but has Thomas Tuchel unfairly overlooked McAtee - and how has he gone from the Forest bench to indispensable?

The City academy graduate made only two Premier League starts last season, one of the bigger victims of Forest's revolving door as the club went through four managers.

Nine starts in Forest's run to the Europa League semi-finals could not hide a campaign of frustration.

It was supposed to be a platform after captaining England Under-21s to Euro 2025 victory, but he played only 289 minutes in the league.

The 24-year-old has already tripled those minutes this season after becoming a key player for Glasner, starting every top-flight game.

It followed the manager suggesting in the summer that McAtee could replace Anderson following his Â£116m move to City - something which left McAtee unsure.

"When I first came in and [Glasner] put me in the [number] six [role] on the second day in my head I was like: 'oh, he's not seeing me in his plans, I'm playing deeper'," he said at Forest's training ground.

"My confidence is growing, but not fully there yet, but I think we're on our way.

"I thought I had it in my locker, but I never thought he would actually try it out with me in pre-season.

"I think Ibra [Sangare] was injured at the time so I was thinking, I'm just going in for Ibra. But then as pre-season got on and I was playing there I felt more comfortable."

Forest fan impressed by 'surprise' player who stepped into Elliot Anderson's shoes

It was evidence of McAtee's work after he worked throughout the summer to return for pre-season.

He trained with former Plymouth, Leeds and Ipswich midfielder David Norris, now a personal trainer, and put on 2.5kg of muscle while losing 1kg of fat.

Weight sessions followed fitness work in the morning, which is what prompted Glasner to credit his summer of work.

The relationship with Glasner has been crucial. The Forest boss has offered clarity and calmness to a squad which endured the chaos last season.

A post-match inquest following the 2-0 defeat by Brentford sparked the right response from the squad, after a start which has left them 16th in the league.

After McAtee failed to find consistency and rhythm last season, Glasner promised him he would be afforded time and the benefit of the doubt if he had a poor game.

"I think [last season] was a me problem. I was struggling to get my chance," he said, having used a psychologist before the start of pre-season.

"I've never really had a season like that, I was always in and out. It was frustrating, but as frustrating as it was, it was a good lesson.

"As I saw my confidence kept going worse and worse and worse. As I've watched clips of me, I can tell when I was going a little bit under.

"This year, if I make a pass and I lose it, it won't bother me as much because I've been through that."

McAtee has always had supporters at the City Ground. All four managers were impressed by his training levels last season, but he was always under pressure to deliver when given a brief chance.

Forest technical director George Syrianos has also championed the calls internally for McAtee.

It has allowed McAtee - whose brother John plays for Bolton - to feel the faith, having learned from previous difficulties, with England on his mind.

He is eager to make the step up to Tuchel's senior side, and has supporters at the Football Association.

He prioritised playing for the U21s at Euro 2025 - captaining them to victory - over going to the Club World Cup with City, and underlined his determination to represent his country to manager Pep Guardiola and director of football Txiki Begiristain at the time.

Now, under Glasner, after a difficult first season, McAtee has that platform with Euro 2028 a realistic target.

"At this moment I need to have a good year for me to maybe be in with the chance of getting picked, but the competition in the position I'm playing is so high," he said.

"If I could add some goals, some stats, it could put me within a chance to be around that circle. The competition is very elite at the moment, but that's the aim, that's the goal."

James McAtee had two previous spells on loan at Sheffield United

Against City, he was moved further forward, with Ryan Yates coming in to add more bodies in midfield.

But the stats back up McAtee's improvement and he compares favourably to others.

He has made the most final-third passes for Forest (151) and has played the joint-most through balls with Morgan Gibbs-White (five). His 426 passes are behind only Murillo's 501, and he has created 18 chances - six short of Gibbs-White.

McAtee is only 29m behind Gibbs-White, having carried the ball 1,180m this season, but has made the most carries with 109 and has won possession back 63 times - winning 53% of his ground duels, indicating he has developed more of a mean streak in his game.

He has comfortably outperformed Everton's James Garner - one of his rivals for a place in the England squad - creating more chances, making more forward passes, winning more defensive duels and making more successful tackles.

McAtee has also made more recoveries, successful tackles, passes and clearances than Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton.

Now, having gone under the radar this season, come the next international break in March, Tuchel may not be able to ignore him.

"I'm seeing this as a different side of myself, I'm so much more confident on the pitch, I'm so much more comfortable," adds McAtee. "It's like two different players."

#804. Euclid space telescope discovers its 1st comet | Space photo of the day for Nov. 16, 2026

The new observatory managed to catch this comet whirling between the orbits of Jupiter and Saturn.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Euclid space telescope has discovered its first comet, called comet C/2026 S1, or comet Euclid for short.

The Euclid mission, a European Space Agency mission that launched in 2023 with contributions from NASA, spotted this previously undetected comet approximately 807 million miles (1.3 billion kilometers) away in observations captured between Sept. 16 and 24.

"I was excited to see my software flag a 'streak' smeared across several images – the result of a fast-moving object. By predicting its position I could identify it in other images, in total finding it in five image sets. Further inspection revealed that it had a fuzzy cloud around it, indicative of an active object like a comet that is shedding dust and gas," Mikko Pöntinen, a scientist at the University of Helsinki who made the initial discovery with a Solar System Objects Science Working Group within the Euclid Consortium, said in a statement.

Following these observations, the team diligently checked current records of comets to ensure that this was, in fact, something new to us.

Euclid is a mission designed to capture long, slow observations of deep space and distant galaxies and collect data to help scientists better unravel the mysteries of dark energy and dark matter. It was in not explicitly designed in any way to capture imagery of fast-moving comet hurtling through our solar system. But still, the space telescoped managed to catch this comet whirling between the orbits of Jupiter and Saturn.

This finding shows that Euclid can be used for more than it was intended, and that in the future scientists could use it to intentionally target other comets in the far reaches of our solar neighborhood. These kinds of observations can also help researchers to identify "noise" like comet trails in Euclid's field of view.

Chelsea Gohd served as a Senior Writer for Space.com from 2018 to 2022 before returning in 2026, covering everything from climate change to planetary science and human spaceflight in both articles and on-camera in videos. With a M.S. in Biology, Chelsea has written and worked for institutions including NASA JPL, the American Museum of Natural History, Scientific American, Discover Magazine Blog, Astronomy Magazine, and Live Science. When not writing, editing or filming something space-y, Gohd is writing music and performing as Foxanne, even launching a song to space in 2021 with Inspiration4. #803. Percy Jackson’s Walker Scobell Reacts to His Dad’s Looks Going Viral

Percy Jackson and the Olympians’ Walker Scobell shared his candid reaction to his dad’s looks going viral in an exclusive interview with E! News.

Some pop culture moments just catch like lightning.

And for Percy Jackson’s Walker Scobell, the innocent decision to bring his (we’ll say it) noticeably handsome dad Pete Scobell along on a Good Morning America appearance Nov. 9 led to whirlwind virality, with “hot dad” memes quickly abounding.

For Walker, however, it’s an internet storm he knows he just needs to weather.

“Oh my god, don’t say it, he’s over there somewhere,” Walker lamented during his exclusive interview with E! News, noting his dad was present in the room. “I'm aware of it. He's aware of it, too. He thought it was hilarious.”

And though Pete didn’t intentionally try to steal his son’s thunder—nor his Master Bolt—Walker joked his dad’s newfound fame is getting to his head.

“He walks, his shoulders are back and he's standing up a little taller,” the 17-year-old quipped, before clarifying, “No, he just thinks it's really funny. I think he's handling it well. He kind of makes a bunch of jokes about it. My mom and my brother and sister were making jokes about it.”

But as it turns out, he isn’t the only young star who found that the public became enamored with the block from whence the chip came.

“I’d actually talked to McKenna Grace about this because her dad has also had a similar treatment online,” Walker revealed. “So, when I saw her for the first time in a couple of years the other day, that was kind of the first thing we said to each other was like, ‘Yeah, our dads.’”

For his costar Tamara Smart—who plays Zeus’ daughter Thalia Grace in the series—the online perception of Pete couldn’t have fallen farther from the actual tree.

“I think it's ironic, too, because he is the most chill, humble guy,” she said. “You just see him hanging around set and he's so sweet. So, to go viral on the morning show is just incredible.”

As for Walker, he’s taking it all in stride. After all, he doesn’t need an oracle to tell him his dad’s looks only bode well for his own future.

“It’s a compliment,” The Adam Project alum affirmed. “Hopefully I’ll look like him.”

But while the actor may have had trouble wrapping his head around his dad’s new claim to fame, he had much more luck getting in touch with his character, Percy Jackson, as he prepared for the third installment of the Disney+ show. After all, he a lot of source material to work with in the form of Rick Riordan’s books.

“I'm lucky because I'm the only character in the show that for these first five books, I know everything that my character is thinking all the time,” Walker explained. “I can always go back to the book and be like, ‘What was he thinking, and what does he think in situations like this?’ So, I feel like I just say what I think he would be thinking out loud or try to show it on my face.”

So, don’t miss Percy Jackson and the Olympians when it hits Disney+ on Nov. 20. And for more electrifying TV to tune into before the end of the year, read on.

Nocturne tells the story of Jonah Lynn (Liev Schreiber), an ex-soldier turned homicide detective who, tired of working the tough streets of Philadelphia, moves to a small town in Western Pennsylvania for a quiet life. But, as the town and his family come under attack from the diabolically cunning serial killer Jurek Walter (Stephen Graham), Jonah must protect all that he holds dear. When the desperate search for Jurek’s last missing victim forces Jonah to send his surrogate daughter FBI Agent Saga Bauer (Zazie Beetz) up against Jurek, how far will Jonah go?

Bertha Russell changed Society at a cost. Now, her family must reckon with the consequences as Agnes van Rhijn seizes an opportunity to regain her position. Meanwhile, Marian forges a new path for herself, and Peggy works to be accepted by her future in-laws. In this new era, you must be careful what you wish for.

St. Denis Medical is a mockumentary about an underfunded, understaffed Oregon hospital where the dedicated doctors and nurses try their best to treat patients while maintaining their own sanity. In season three, romantic entanglements and personal struggles complicate relationships in the Emergency Department, pushing some St. Denis employees to the brink.

The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins (NBC) - Nov. 2

Season two of the hit comedy returns with the unlikely duo of former football star Reggie Dinkins (Tracy Morgan) and documentarian Arthur Tobin (Daniel Radcliffe), both still chasing redemption and still making a mess of it. With the help of his family, Reggie will continue his quest to recapture his past glory.

In season two, Santi takes the next step in his pursuit of professional golf, only to discover how quickly the game changes when talent becomes expectation. As Santi chases his dream, Pryce Cahill (Owen Wilson) finds himself wondering what might still be possible for him. Urged on by his former rival Clark Ross (Timothy Olyphant), Pryce does something nobody expects: he bets on himself, launching an improbable comeback in hopes of becoming the oldest golfer ever to win a major. But the road back proves far harder than he imagined. And the closer Pryce gets to the golfer he once was, the more he is forced to confront why he never fulfilled the promise everyone once saw in him. With brilliant new coach Amanda (Rhea Seehorn) and trusted caddie Mitts (Marc Maron) in his corner, Pryce sets out to prove — to the golf world and, more importantly, to himself — that maybe he really was as good as everyone always said he was.

The lawyers of Grant, Ronson & Greene are back for another season of scandals, secrets, and stilettos. As new allegiances form, friendships are tested and a shocking revelation threatens the very existence of the firm.

The Remarried Princess (Hulu & Disney+) - Nov. 4

Based on the hit Naver Webtoon of the same name, The Remarried Empress follows the strained relationship of beloved Empress Navier and her husband Emperor Sovieshu of the Eastern Kingdom. With anxieties rising across the kingdom, the couple’s relationship begins to fracture when Sovieshu falls in love with a runaway slave and attempts to move heaven and earth to win her heart. Unwilling to compromise her dignity, Navier acquiesces to the emperor’s requests on one condition – that she be allowed to remarry rival Crown Prince Heinrey of the Western Kingdom. What follows is a tale of love, lust and regret that threatens the fate of an entire kingdom as Navier strives to reclaim her power.

The documentary traces Muhammad Ali’s coming of age story, following a young Cassius Clay through the personal, professional and political battles he fought inside and outside the ring. Set against a changing America, The Greatest follows a once-in-a-generation talent fighting for the right to become his own man. Through the fights that made him a champion and the convictions that made him an icon, a young man from Louisville transforms himself into Muhammad Ali, the greatest of all time.

Taken: Natalee Holloway (Netflix) - Nov. 4

On May 30, 2005, 18-year-old Natalee Holloway vanished on a high school graduation trip to Aruba—and never came home. What followed was years of unanswered questions, a missing teenager, and a mother's relentless fight for the truth. Now, over 20 years later, Natalee's mother, Beth, is ready to tell the complete story. With exclusive, unprecedented access to Beth and those who were with Natalee when she vanished, this three-part documentary series is the definitive account of a case that gripped a nation and never let go. It's a story of a mother who refused to stop searching, an investigation that spanned continents, and a daughter whose memory endures. This is Natalee's story, told at last in full.

Helen (Keira Knightley) is still betraying her nation’s secrets to the covert organization she serves: the Black Doves. But after the misadventures of last Christmas, and with her husband Wallace (Andrew Buchan), preparing to become Prime Minister, she is walking a more treacherous line than ever.

Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook (Apple TV) - Nov. 6

The eight-episode series follows Nora Lum, aka Awkwafina, on a cross-country culinary road trip as she attempts to revive her family’s beloved Chinese restaurant.

Wolves Up Close With Bertie Gregory (National Geographic) - Nov. 6

Reconnecting with a pack of wolves he has followed for seven years, Bertie Gregory sets out to capture one of the Arctic’s most dangerous and rarely filmed hunts: wolves taking on a bull moose, prey roughly ten times their size. Led by Kona, a striking white breeding male, the pack faces a critical winter as dwindling food supplies, an encroaching rival wolf and an aging leader threaten its survival.

Charmed By a Southern Monster (Peacock) - Nov. 9

Starring Craig Conover as Hunter Caldwell and Nicole Mattox as Maeve Marchant, the series blends soapy romance, workplace rivalry and small-town mystery.

The story follows Maeve, a brilliant corporate fixer sent to convince and seduce Hunter, a rumored murderer, into selling his family’s estate. But when she discovers that the town’s most feared man may actually be its most misunderstood, and the only person who can protect her from her dangerous ex-boyfriend, Maeve becomes entangled in Hunter’s world. As family secrets and a billion-dollar development deal threaten to unravel their growing connection, she must confront her past and decide how much she’s willing to risk for love.

Whitney Way Thore is stepping into a transformative new chapter. Back in her home state of North Carolina, Whitney has found love with Jake, a man she first met years ago before reconnecting after her return to Charlotte. As their relationship deepens, Whitney is rediscovering her confidence through dance, exploring new possibilities on her health journey, and taking meaningful steps toward the future she’s always wanted, including her biggest dream of becoming a mom.

Picking up after the gut-wrenching mid-series finale, Tony Baddingham and Declan O'Hara's battle for the Cotswolds crown reaches fever pitch, while Rupert Campbell-Black is forced to confront his own personal demons. Against a backdrop of hedonistic parties, Bonfire Night chaos, the Hampshire Hunt Ball and a turbulent Christmas, affairs unravel, alliances fracture and rivalries intensify. Caught in the middle of the frenzied franchise war, Taggie O'Hara must find the courage to follow her heart, while those around her face the consequences of ambition, power and secrets that can no longer remain hidden. But as series two draws to a close, who will get their happy ending?

From Ron Howard, the documentary explores the life, career, and cultural impact of legendary American photographer Richard Avedon.

The Good Daughter is a suspenseful thriller wrapped in a deeply emotional story about love, family and resilience. Sisters Charlotte (Meghann Fahy) and Samantha (Rose Byrne) Quinn have spent the last 20 years trying to piece together the lives that were fractured by a single night of violence. When another attack splinters the small town of Pikeville, Charlotte – now a lawyer like her father – is the first witness on the scene. As the case unfolds and twists through painful memories and buried secrets, what emerges is not just a story of survival, but of enduring ties between a father and his daughters, and the complex bond between sisters.

After a reunion where the status of friendships and situationships remained ambiguous, the Charmers are determined to define their relationships and mend wounds. However, when true feelings bubble up and juicy rumors catch fire, the group seeks to unveil the truth – even if it costs them more than just friendships.

Three years into their jobs as response officers, Constables Grace Ellis, Tommy Foster, and Annie Conlon are operating at their limit, facing a new threat on the streets that the police can barely control. Meanwhile the murder trial of Gerry Cliff exposes a dangerous and long-buried secret that leads to chaos both inside the police, and across the criminal underworld. As they grapple with big decisions about their future, Grace, Tommy and Annie must find the courage to face the greatest threat they have ever encountered: the truth.

Each episode of the drama unfolds across three timelines of a heist: the 12 months of planning, the 12 hours of the heist, and the 12 days following the heist. The series follows a disgraced FBI agent (Anthony Mackie) and an American career criminal (Jamie Dornan) who play a zero-sum game of cat and mouse across Europe. At the center of it all is the daring, epic raid on a bank vault deep beneath the streets of Zurich.

Expedition: Saving Our Seas (National Geographic) - Nov. 13

The documentary follows teams of National Geographic Explorers as they investigate our global Ocean, from seashore to seafloor and pole to pole. Combining cutting-edge technology with the knowledge of coastal communities, they chase the discoveries and solutions needed to protect our Oceans at a critical moment.

Homicide for the Holidays (Oxygen) - Nov. 14

The holidays are supposed to be the most wonderful time of the year. But for some families, cherished celebrations become the backdrop for unimaginable violence. Season six of Homicide For The Holidays brings a new batch of deadly deeds to the supposed jolliest time of the year as investigators pursue those responsible and seek justice for families shattered at a time meant for togetherness.

Diane Morgan returns as Philomena Cunk in a new series from Charlie Brooker. Billed as Cunk's most glamorous outing yet, she charts the history of cinema, from the invention of the camera and the New Wave filmmakers of the 1960s right up to the entrance of CGI and what the future of AI holds. Cunk will attempt to demystify it all while sitting in lumpy seats with stale popcorn, asking herself where did cinema come from? And why? What does it want? And why can’t it tell us?

Small Town Trouble: Texas (Bravo) - Nov. 18

Set in Boerne (pronounced "Bur-nee"), Texas, the series follows a charming yet unconventional group of wives, mothers and social insiders – Aaryn Williams, Alli McAnelly, Annari Uys, Gabby Hernandez Huffman, and Hailey Head, alongside their respective husbands – as conservative values of small-town life collide with forbidden attraction, messy friendships, and shocking   secrets. Here, perception is everything, temptation is everywhere, and the truth is never as buttoned-up as it looks.

The story of Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison, two hyper-smart, ambitious young idealists who tried to remake the global financial system in the blink of an eye - before they were accused of stealing $8 billion and became Gen Z's own Bonnie & Clyde.

Nelly and Ashanti: We Belong Together (Peacock) - Nov. 19

This season, Ashanti continues to balance motherhood, continuing to perform on stage, and taking control of her musical legacy. While navigating living in St. Louis and New York City, Ashanti also juggles re-recording her debut album to retain her masters, finding time for her girlfriends who keep her grounded, and recording new music with some of music's hottest artists. After years of nonstop touring, Nelly reflects on the physical toll it’s taking at this stage in his life, and an unexpected family loss reminds him what matters most. Between raising their son, honoring their village, and planning for their future, Nelly and Ashanti discover that belonging together isn’t about standing still; it’s about building a future on their own terms.

Nearly a decade after a mysterious female jogger dubbed “The Mad Pooper” captured national attention for repeatedly defecating on residential lawns across Colorado Springs, one of the strangest unsolved mysteries is back in the spotlight. In the new two-hour special, viewers will dive headfirst into the bizarre true story that left an entire community searching for answers and asking one simple question: why?

As the survivors race to bury their sins before rescue arrives and an old flame roars back into town with plans of her own, turns out not every homecoming is a joyous one, and this one's going to sting.

Adapted from Tom Bradby's bestselling novel, Secret Service follows senior MI6 officer Kate Henderson (Gemma Arterton), whose covert investigation uncovers evidence that a high-ranking U.K. politician may be working as a Russian asset. With trust shattered and her career on the line, Kate must navigate the shifting sands of political loyalty, international threat, and personal sacrifice as she races to uncover their identity before it's too late.

The new comedy follows a team of dedicated archaeologists (and less-dedicated college students) who spend their summer working on a dig site in Greece. Their discovery of a rare artifact sends them on the adventure of a lifetime.
